releases.title: The Conformance Sprint
releases.summary: A major polish pass that resolves the P0-P2 issue backlog, ensuring Chonkline speaks the IRC protocol correctly for strict clients like BitchX.
highlights: Fixed malformed MODE broadcasts for operator (+o) and voice (+v) to prevent client parsing errors
Added a proper MOTD with correct start codes (375) to stop BitchX from crashing
Corrected RPL_USERHOST (302) responses to include the full user@host format
Fixed NOTICE delivery and CTCP replies so private messages reach the right users
Trimmed unnecessary closing lines from the MOTD for a cleaner welcome experience

releases.title: Identity & Accounts
releases.summary: Chonkline now supports modern user identification with SASL accounts, host cloaking, and proper server naming.
highlights: Added SASL authentication and account support for persistent identity
Enabled host cloaking to protect user privacy
Introduced IRCv3 capabilities for better client feature detection
Added ChanServ channel registration for persistent channel management
Configurable server identity via IRC_SERVER_NAME and proper host reporting (002)

releases.title: Secure & Stable Connections
releases.summary: Improved connection security and stability with TLS support and robust handling of MODE changes and queries.
highlights: Enabled TLS connections on port 6697 via a ghostunnel sidecar
Fixed MODE ban-list queries to return accurate results
Ensured MODE changes are properly broadcast to channel members
Deployed fixes for strict client compatibility regarding numerics and server identity

releases.title: Handshake & Reconnect Hardening
releases.summary: The initial connection and reconnection process is smoother, with better handling of capabilities, pings, and nicknames.
highlights: Fixed CAP negotiation to prevent handshake timeouts
Added client PING/PONG handling to keep connections alive
Improved nick validation and fast nick reclaim after disconnects
Harden reconnect logic with keepalive signals and CAP-END gating

releases.title: First Light
releases.summary: The initial release of Chonkline, establishing the core protocol behavior that makes channels feel right.
highlights: Echoes your own JOIN and PART messages so client channel buffers open correctly
Fixed error numerics to target the correct user
Implemented ghost reaping to clean up stale user entries
Complete registration burst for a faster initial connection
